S1.why: S1 marks the slots, so the plain adjective "gratis" is enough. It works as a label and fits the 12-character budget.

S2.why: An invitation in the imperative with du. It also reads right when nothing is saved yet, where "Fortsätt spara" would not.

S3.s: Du har använt alla %lld gratis cutlings. De är fortsatt gratis och fungerar som vanligt.
S3.back: You have used all %lld free cutlings. They are continuedly free and work as usual.
S3.why: "fortsatt gratis" is the everyday Swedish way to say something stays free. Lowercase "cutlings" in a sentence, as in the vocabulary sentence.

S4.why: "ingår" is how Swedish states what comes with something. Avoids a "Du kan…" sentence under an imperative title.

S5.s: Du har använt %lld av dina %lld gratis cutlings.
S5.back: You have used %lld of your %lld free cutlings.
S5.why: Swedish keeps the same number order (used, then total), so plain %lld twice. Uses du/dina as in the vocabulary file.

S6.why: "Plats för" is the natural noun phrase for capacity. Fits one line with "5 000".

S7.s: Spara upp till %@ texter och %lld bilder.
S7.back: Save up to %@ texts and %lld images.
S7.why: Plural "texter" for text items. "bilder" comes from the vocabulary file.

S8.why: Swedish lists three things with "och" and no comma before it.

S9.s: Ett köp gäller på alla dina enheter med samma Apple-konto.
S9.back: One purchase applies on all your devices with same Apple-account.
S9.why: "Apple-konto" and "enheter" come from the vocabulary sentence. "gäller" is the normal verb for what a purchase covers.

S10.why: Plain verb phrase. Nothing comes back each month.

S11.s: Ingen prenumeration, ingen reklam och ingen registrering.
S11.back: No subscription, no advertising and no registration.
S11.why: "registrering" instead of "konto", so it does not clash with the Apple-konto in S9. "och" before the last item, with no comma.

S12.why: The standard Swedish wording Swedish iOS apps use for the App Store restore action.

S13.why: Present tense of the same verb, ending with the ellipsis character.

S14.why: "Lås upp" is the Swedish App Store verb. "för" plus the price is how Swedish buttons state a price. "Paying once" is already said in S10.

S15.why: S14 with the price removed, so the button only gains the price when it loads.

S16.why: The usual Swedish way to put something off politely. It postpones and does not refuse.

S17.why: The verb iOS in Swedish uses on close buttons.

S18.why: "Nu" comes first, which gives the line its pride and warmth. Singular "ditt" matches du.

S19.s: Tack för köpet. Du stöttar Cutling och den enda personen bakom appen.
S19.back: Thanks for the-purchase. You support Cutling and the only person behind the-app.
S19.why: "Tack för köpet" is what a Swedish shop says. "stöttar" is warmer than "stöder".

S20.s: Välkommen tillbaka. Ditt tidigare köp är återställt.
S20.back: Welcome back. Your earlier purchase is restored.
S20.why: A greeting, then the fact. "återställt" repeats the verb from S12.

S21.why: VoiceOver reads it as a full clause. The plural agreement "använda" is right because the noun is the plural "cutlings".

S22.s: Antal cutlings: %lld. Nu finns det plats för %@.
S22.back: Number cutlings: %lld. Now exists it room for %@.
S22.why: "Antal cutlings:" keeps the noun out of agreement with the number, so 1, 2, 5 and 21 all read correctly.

S23.s: Cutling är upplåst. Nu finns det plats för %@ cutlings.
S23.back: Cutling is unlocked. Now exists it room for %@ cutlings.
S23.why: "upplåst" is the past participle of "låsa upp", the same verb as on the button. Capital C means the app here, and lowercase "cutlings" means the items.

S24.why: The everyday idiom for a payment that did not complete. It blames no one.

S25.s: App Store går inte att nå just nu. Försök igen om en stund.
S25.back: App Store goes not to reach just now. Try again in a while.
S25.why: "går inte att nå" is the natural impersonal form. "om en stund" means shortly, without urgency.

S27.s: Apple-kontot på den här enheten har inget tidigare köp av Cutling.
S27.back: The-Apple-account on this here device has no earlier purchase of Cutling.
S27.why: Makes the account the subject, which avoids a long relative clause and keeps the line under 80 characters. "Apple-konto" comes from the vocabulary file.

S28.s: Gratisversionen rymmer %lld cutlings. Lås upp Cutling en gång, så kan du spara så många du vill.
S28.back: The-free-version holds %lld cutlings. Unlock Cutling one time, so can you save as many you want.
S28.why: "rymmer" is the verb for capacity. The "…, så kan du…" construction is how a Swede would say it aloud to Siri.

S29.why: A compact label under the list title, in the same shape as S1.

K1.why: The compound "gratisplatser" names the slots clearly in 37 characters. "Lås upp" names what the tap does.

M1.why: A verb-led window title, the way Swedish macOS names command windows.

M2.why: M1 with the ellipsis character, because the button opens a window.

M3.why: A sentence-case row label, as Swedish macOS Settings writes them.

M4.why: "av" is the Swedish compact pair, as in "3 av 5".

M5.why: The same participle as in S23.

M6.s: Ett köp låser upp Cutling på iPhone, iPad och Mac.
M6.back: One purchase unlocks Cutling on iPhone, iPad and Mac.
M6.why: Same device list as S8. Present tense states a fact.

M7.s: Upplåst på iPhone, iPad och Mac med det här Apple-kontot.
M7.back: Unlocked on iPhone, iPad and Mac with this here Apple-account.
M7.why: Swedish says "det här" for this one. "Apple-kontot" is the definite form of the vocabulary word.

M8.s: Du köpte Cutling innan den blev gratis, så den förblir upplåst. Tack för att du var med från start.
M8.back: You bought Cutling before it became free, so it remains unlocked. Thanks for that you were with from start.
M8.why: "den" refers to the app (en app). "var med från start" is a warm Swedish way to thank an early supporter.
